correctness.rationale: A unit-length sliding window always has Poisson(λ) marginal. For overlap λJ_v(t), the two-window Poisson generating function is exp(λJ_v zu) after Charlier centering, giving exact diagonal covariance delta_rs r!λ^r J_v^r. Orthogonal L² expansion and Tonelli give a finite nonnegative infinite variance series; one-dependent stationary integrals across integer time periods establish CLT and variance for merely L² observables. Average_t J_v=1-v; convex Jensen makes uniform η minimal, with strictness for every nonzero higher Charlier component and every nonconstant Fourier mode of η. For h=(n)_2, the r=1,2 modes and Parseval reproduce the exact published Fourier penalty; for h=n variance is λ. Independently checked Charlier covariance at λ=3/2 and overlap=2/5 (exact 153/25) and harmonic penalty numerically.
residual_risks: The claim uses deterministic one-unit windows, normalized bounded positive periodic η and physical-time averages; the quadratic formula is earlier coverage, not new.

value.rationale: The practically motivated open question is whether arbitrary nonlinear count observables lose efficiency under periodic modulation even when the Poisson target and linear estimator remain unchanged. Extending a known single quadratic Fourier penalty to an exact positive Charlier-spectrum formula for ALL Poisson L² observables and an iff affine equality characterization is a mathematically useful design principle, not a routine re-labeling of the quadratic formula.
residual_risks: No implication for non-Poisson targets, event-clock efficiency or multivariate interacting samplers.
